key_insight: Serum brain-derived tau (BD-tau) distinguished traumatic brain injury (TBI) from spinal cord injury (SCI), highlighting its potential as an injury-specific blood biomarker.
clinical_relevance: If validated, serum BD-tau could support acute neurotrauma differentiation and injury-specific trial enrollment; this study does not address AI or cancer drug discovery.
method: Measured baseline serum BD-tau across multiple cohorts comprising 285 TBI patients, 57 SCI patients, and 22 controls.
Compared discrimination with paired cerebrospinal fluid measurements and established blood biomarkers.
Tracked serum BD-tau trajectories for up to 144 hours post-injury.
evidence_signal: Baseline serum BD-tau distinguished TBI from SCI with AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.96), while separate comparisons favored serum over cerebrospinal fluid and established blood biomarkers.
watch_item: Performance in mixed brain–spinal injuries and broader acute-care populations, along with actionable diagnostic thresholds, requires further validation.
paper_title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
